style.vernacular: Rebuilt after 1944: flat-roofed reinforced-concrete buildings of one to four storeys, cream, white and pastel painted render, with taller resort hotels along Beach Road in Garapan; typhoon-hardened low-rise, corrugated metal roofs on houses and sheds, scattered Japanese-era coral-concrete ruins and shrines; limestone terraces, flame trees, coconut palms and tangantangan scrub.
style.ornament: Japanese-era Shinto and memorial forms (torii gates, komainu guardian statues, stone lanterns, peace bells, hexagonal prayer halls); Spanish and German colonial church heritage; hotel porte-cocheres with pastel bands; Chamorro latte stones as a recurring motif.
